CSN-212: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
(Spring 2015-2016)

B. Tech. (CSE) II Year

Course Instructor: Sudip Roy

Teaching Assistants: Ankur Gupta (PhD Student), Smit Parsania (IDD Student), Manish Kumar Dixit (MTech II Year Student), Rupesh Kumar (MTech II Year Student), Surendra Meena (MTech II Year Student)

 

Important Announcements

  • Class will start from January 11, 2016.
  • Form your group in Moodle. Each group can have at most TWO students.

 

Course Outline

  • This is a course of Four (4) credit.
  • It consists of Three (3) lecture hours per week and One (1) hour tutorial for each of the TWO sub-batches.
  • The basic thrust of the course would be to familiarize students with the design strategies and bounds on the performance of different computer algorithms.
  • We will try cover all the topics as given in Syllabus, but in a more structured or modular fashion. We may also deviate a bit from the syllabus.
  • Prerequisite: CSN-102 (Data Structures).
  • Performance Evaluation: Class Work Sessional (CWS) = 25%, Mid-Term Exam (MTE) = 25%, End-Term Exam (ETE) = 50%.
  • CWS (25% marks) will be computed by a weighted sum of different components.

Study Materials

Books:
[B1] Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Lieserson, Ronald L. Rivest and Clifford Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, Second Edition, MIT Press/McGraw-Hill, 2009.
[B2] Jon Kleinberg and Éva Tardos, Algorithm Design, Pearson, 2005.
[B3] Anany Levitin, Introduction to The Design and Analysis of Algorithm, III edition, Pearson, 2011.
[B4] Sanjoy Dasgupta, Christos Papadimitriou, Umesh Vazirani, “Algorithms”, Tata McGraw-Hill. 2008.

References:
[R1] Lecture notes by Prof. David Mount, Department of Computer Science, University of Maryland, USA.
[R2] Lecture notes by Prof. Sandeep Sen, Department of Computer Science & Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, India.
